title: Utamaro, Picture Book of Selected Insects (Ehon mushi erabi)
lede: A two-volume color-printed book in which Kitagawa Utamaro’s insects and plants face comic poems on the opposite page, inside thin printed frames.
summary: Insects and plants in soft flat color beside vertical poems, inside a ruled frame. Kitagawa Utamaro, 1788.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Art Institute of Chicago image of 2022.633 (1686 × 1331 px). The image shows one open spread; other spreads were not inspected.

styles.note: A color-printed picture book (ehon): the same key-block line and flat block colors as single-sheet prints, with text and picture sharing a framed page.

context: AIC catalogues the work as color woodblock printed books, two volumes, 27 × 18.3 cm, 1788. [AIC 2022.633](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/220320).
Wikipedia’s Ukiyo-e article names illustrated books among the formats of ukiyo-e production. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukiyo-e).
observed: The open spread has two pages, each with a thin double-ruled frame printed in black.
On the left page a katydid sits on a large dark purple eggplant among olive-green leaves and pale pink flowers. The plant sits on the lower edge of the frame and leaves the upper half empty.
The plant continues across the gutter to the right page, where a snail climbs a stem.
On the right page, poems in cursive script run in vertical columns from the upper right.
Colors are flat and muted: dark purple, olive green, pale pink, and buff. Fine black lines draw the veins, the legs, and the antennae.
The paper is cream with a visible laid texture.
interpretation: The book shows how the style handles text and image together: one frame for both, text in a column, picture in the lower half.
The picture that crosses the gutter treats the spread as one composition.
borrow: Put the image low in a ruled frame and run the text in a column above or beside it.
Let one element cross the boundary between two panels to join them.

images.alt: Open book spread with thin black-ruled frames. Left: a katydid on a large dark purple eggplant with leaves and pale flowers. Right: a snail on a flowering stem and vertical columns of cursive poems.
images.caption: Kitagawa Utamaro, Picture Book of Selected Insects (Ehon mushi erabi), 1788. [Art Institute of Chicago 2022.633](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/220320), Frederick W. Gookin Collection. CC0.

rights.statement: The Art Institute of Chicago marks the object public domain (`is_public_domain: true`) and releases images of public-domain works under CC0. [AIC open access](https://www.artic.edu/open-access/open-access-images). Utamaro died in 1806, and the book was published in 1788, so the work is public domain in Japan and the United States.
